spread: Christian Gospel textual and interpretive traditions

earliest_attestation.value: commonly dated within ca. 65–75 CE scholarly range for Mark

narrative.summary: In Mark 13:2, Jesus is portrayed as telling a disciple that the Temple's great buildings will be thrown down so completely that no stone remains upon another. Later readers compare this wording with the Roman destruction of Jerusalem and the Second Temple in 70 CE. MFTL treats the wording as textual attestation and the text–event connection as an interpretive historical comparison; it does not infer supernatural fulfillment from the historical event alone.
narrative.long_description: RGBL supplies the exact SBLGNT and World English Bible passage identities. LEGEND owns the independently evidenced 70 CE destruction event. SUPERHERO owns human witness/recorder intelligence such as Flavius Josephus. The dating of Mark relative to 70 CE remains a scholarly question, so this record intentionally separates the existence of a prediction narrative from claims about its historical timing, authorship, or supernatural fulfillment.
